summary:
MARS MAPS is an interactive 2D and 3D planetary exploration and mission-planning web platform built using real NASA orbital datasets (MOLA topography, Viking MDIM 2.1, and OpenPlanetaryMap).

​To address the challenge of planning safe human and robotic missions on Mars, our platform transforms complex planetary data into actionable survival tools. Users can inspect real-time MOLA altitude and atmospheric pressure via NASA’s barometric formula, toggle 13 environmental layers with real-world kilometer dimensions, and explore a 360° 3D Mars globe featuring live Phobos and Deimos orbits. Beyond visualization, MARS MAPS includes a Custom Base Habitability Simulator, a Route Builder with automated terrain and communications-blackout hazard detection, a Side-by-Side Site Comparator, an ISRU resource calculator, and survival simulations for dust storms and solar flares.

​This project is vital because it bridges the gap between landing on Mars and sustaining human life there safely.
details:
MARS MAPS is an interactive 2D and 3D planetary exploration and mission-planning web application powered by real NASA datasets (MOLA topography, Viking MDIM 2.1, and OpenPlanetaryMap). By clicking any coordinate on Mars, the app computes exact MOLA elevation and atmospheric pressure using NASA’s barometric formula to determine parachute landing feasibility. Users can toggle active rovers, candidate landing zones (such as Arcadia Planitia), lava tube bunkers, hazard zones, and 13 environmental layers with real-world kilometer dimensions, as well as switch to a 360° 3D Mars Globe with live Phobos and Deimos orbits.

​Engineering & Survival Tools

Beyond visualization, MARS MAPS acts as a tactical mission-control suite featuring:

​Custom Base Habitability Simulator: Evaluates any site on a 0–100 scale based on pressure, solar irradiance, and proximity to subsurface water ice.

​Route Builder & Hazard Analysis: Scans custom expedition paths for steep scarps, boulder fields, radiation zones, and communications blackouts.

​Site Comparator & ISRU Calculator: Compares landing sites side by side and calculates metric tons of oxygen, water, and methane propellant required for crewed missions.

​Contingency & Day/Night Simulations: Models global dust storms, solar flare radiation spikes, and the real-time Martian solar terminator.

​Benefits & Expected Impact

MARS MAPS democratizes planetary science and mission engineering, serving both as an educational tool for students and a rapid prototyping environment for mission planners. It bridges the gap between raw orbital telemetry and actionable human survival decisions.

​Tools, Languages & Software Used

Built with HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), integrating Leaflet.js for high-resolution 2D GIS mapping, Three.js for WebGL 3D planetary rendering, and NASA/USGS planetary tile services.

​Creativity & Team Considerations

Rather than building a static map viewer, our team combined GIS telemetry, real-time physics formulas, and crisis simulation into a single lightweight browser tool—with zero installation required. We prioritized scientific accuracy (real kilometer scales, barometric physics, and actual rover/landing coordinates), intuitive UX, and full accessibility across desktop and mobile devices.
